notes: 2025-26 Topps Chrome base set, LA Lakers. Printed name is REAVES (not Reeves). Card is in a penny sleeve, photographed sideways, with glare across the right of the frame and a hard white/wood background edge that the quad detector could mistake for the card. The collector number is not on the front — expect it missing rather than wrong unless something invents one. No insert (base card), so `insert` is unasserted.

2025-26 Topps Chrome 'Ball of Duty' insert, Detroit Pistons. Same sleeve/rotation/glare conditions. Insert code BD11 is not on the front, but the insert name is printed large. Product goes in setName, treatment in insert.

2023-24 Donruss Rated Rookie, Memphis Grizzlies. First fixture in a rigid magnetic holder rather than a penny sleeve, first held in hand (fingers and a blurred room in frame rather than a flat surface), first non-Topps manufacturer, and first parallel. The parallel is the point: base and Red Laser Holo share name, set, number and year but are worth very different amounts, so missing it misprices the listing. Expect `parallel` to come back missing unless CardSight returns a trustworthy exact match — OCR has no field that reaches it. Name asserted with the 'II' suffix as printed; if catalogues return 'GG Jackson' this will score wrong, which is a decision to make on the evidence rather than by loosening matching up front. `cardNumber` unasserted (it is on the back).

FIRST GRADED SLAB and FIRST SCREENSHOT — this is a phone screenshot of an eBay listing page, not a photo of a card, so it tests something different from the rest. The card image sits small inside browser chrome, and the listing title ('2024 Obsidian Orbital Molten Gold /10 LEBRON JAMES #16 PSA 10 POP 2') is legible text in the frame, so a model can score well here by reading the page rather than the card. Treat a good result as evidence about screenshots, not about card reading. Rectification will likely fail or crop to the wrong rectangle — a screenshot is full of them. NOTE THE YEAR: the PSA label reads '2024 OBSIDIAN', a single year, which contradicts the season convention used for the Topps Chrome fixtures; the label is authoritative for a graded card. certNumber matters most here — it is looked up against PSA's API, so a wrong one returns a different card's grade and population.
